skill.name: axe-ios-simulator
skill.description: Guide agents through AXe CLI commands for iOS Simulator taps, gestures, text input, screenshots, video capture, and accessibility inspection.
skill.summary: Automates iOS Simulator interaction and inspection with AXe CLI command guidance.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documentation-only AXe iOS Simulator guide, with no prompt injection or hidden malicious instructions found. Several static findings are real external-command or simulator data-capture risks because the skill teaches agents to install AXe, drive simulator input, record screens, and inspect accessibility output. Many other findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, headings, or ordinary simulator control commands mislabeled as system reconnaissance.

remediation.issue: External AXe and Homebrew commands are presented for direct execution.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to confirm the target simulator UDID and obtain user approval before installation or simulator control commands run.

remediation.issue: Screenshots, video, streams, and accessibility output can expose simulator app data.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to avoid real credentials, private records, or production accounts while capturing simulator evidence.

remediation.issue: The form filling example includes a password-like sample value.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the sample value with an obvious placeholder and state that real passwords should not be typed into shared recordings or screenshots.

static_findings.snippet: Press `Ctrl+C` to stop recording. AXe finalizes MP4 and prints path to stdout.

content.value_statement: Manual simulator interaction slows mobile development and QA review. This skill provides AXe CLI guidance for taps, gestures, text input, screenshots, video, and accessibility inspection.
actual_capabilities: Install AXe with Homebrew and list available iOS Simulators.
Tap simulator elements by coordinates, accessibility identifier, or label.
Run gestures, swipes, low-level touches, and simulator hardware buttons.
Enter text from direct input, stdin, files, HID keycodes, or key sequences.
Capture screenshots, record MP4 video, and stream simulator video output.
Inspect the accessibility tree or metadata for a specific screen point.
limitations: Requires macOS, Xcode iOS Simulator, and the AXe CLI.
Targets iOS Simulator workflows, not physical device automation.
Commands can alter simulator state and capture visible app data.
Provides command guidance, not a complete test runner or assertion framework.

use_cases.title: Run UI Smoke Checks
use_cases.description: Drive common simulator flows with taps, typing, gestures, and buttons during local development.

use_cases.title: Capture Bug Evidence
use_cases.description: Create screenshots or videos after a reproducible simulator action for QA reports.

use_cases.title: Inspect Accessibility State
use_cases.description: Review accessibility labels, identifiers, and point metadata before improving app UI automation.

prompt_templates.title: List Simulators
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AXe iOS Simulator skill to show me how to list simulators and choose the correct UDID.

prompt_templates.title: Tap And Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to tap the Email field, type sample text, tap Continue, and wait for the next screen.

prompt_templates.title: Record Reproduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to record a short simulator video while I reproduce a bug, then stop recording and report the saved file path.

prompt_templates.title: Find Element By Scrolling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe accessibility inspection and scrolling to find a target element, tap it, and capture a result screenshot.

output_examples.input: Find the active simulator and capture its current screen.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists simulators, confirms the selected UDID, runs a screenshot capture, and reports the saved image path.

output_examples.input: Fill a test login form in the simulator.
output_examples.output: The assistant taps fields by accessible labels, enters sample non-sensitive values, submits the form, and waits for the next state.

output_examples.input: Check what accessibility data is available at one screen point.
output_examples.output: The assistant requests the point coordinates, runs the inspection command, and summarizes the returned label and element metadata.

best_practices: Confirm the target simulator UDID before running any command.
Prefer accessibility identifiers or labels over fixed coordinates when they are available.
Review screenshots, videos, and accessibility output for sensitive data before sharing.
anti_patterns: Running commands against an unspecified or wrong simulator instance.
Recording screens while real credentials or private data are visible.
Depending only on fixed coordinates for layouts that change by device size.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps agents use AXe CLI commands for iOS Simulator taps, gestures, typing, screenshots, video, and accessibility inspection.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.

faq.question: Does it control physical iOS devices?
faq.answer: No. The documented commands target iOS Simulator automation through AXe.

faq.question: Can it inspect accessibility labels?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commands to describe the full UI tree or inspect metadata at a screen point.

faq.question: Can it record simulator video?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents MP4 recording, MJPEG streaming, and ffmpeg piping examples.

faq.question: What should users confirm before running commands?
faq.answer: Users should confirm AXe is installed, the simulator UDID is correct, and no sensitive data is visible.
